akhfash:4-4.t: He said ﴿إِن تَتُوبَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا﴾: He made it (قلوب, "hearts") plural because they are two out of two. «[Translator's note: i.e., one heart belonging to each of two persons; such a pair is expressed with the plural.]»

akhfash:12-12.t: And He said ﴿وَمَرْيَمَ ٱبْنَةَ عِمْرَانَ﴾ and ﴿ٱمْرَأَةَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ on the construction: "And Allah set forth the wife of Pharaoh and Mary as an example" (وَضَرَبَ اللهُ امْرَأَةَ فِرْعَونَ وَمَرْيَمَ مَثَلا).

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ «يا» is a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), and «ها» is for drawing attention (tanbīh); ﴿النَّبِيُّ﴾ a badal (substitute) for «أيّها»; ﴿لِمَ﴾ the lām is a preposition, and «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of a genitive (majrūr) governed by the lām, and both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb after them; ﴿تُحَرِّمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿لَكَ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿تَبْتَغِي مَرْضاتَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being latent, and the clause is circumstantial (a ḥāl). ﴿أَزْواجِكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct). ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its two khabars (predicates), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿قَدْ فَرَضَ اللَّهُ﴾ «قد» is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq), and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿تَحِلَّةَ أَيْمانِكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), annexed (muḍāf), and «أيمانكم» is muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿اللَّهُ مَوْلاكُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿أَسَرَّ النَّبِيُّ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿إِلى بَعْضِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿أَزْواجِهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿حَدِيثاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; ﴿لما﴾ an adverb of time with conditional meaning, not making the verb jussive; ﴿نَبَّأَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); ﴿بِهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is in the position of a genitive by iḍāfa; ﴿وَأَظْهَرَهُ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the Name of Majesty being its fāʿil; ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَرَّفَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; ﴿بَعْضَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَأَعْرَضَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «عرف»; ﴿عَنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; ﴿لما﴾ its i'rab has been given before; ﴿نَبَّأَها﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being latent; ﴿بِهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is in the position of a genitive by iḍāfa. ﴿قالَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position. ﴿مَنْ﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَنْبَأَكَ﴾ a past verb and its first object, the fāʿil being latent; ﴿هذا﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, and the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of «من», and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿نَبَّأَنِيَ الْعَلِيمُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, «العليم» being its fāʿil; ﴿الْخَبِيرُ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), and the clause is the object of the saying.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿إِنْ تَتُوبا﴾ a conditional particle making the verb jussive, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, the alif being the fāʿil (agent); ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿فَقَدْ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of reason (taʿlīl); ﴿قد صَغَتْ﴾ a particle of realisation (taḥqīq) and a past verb; ﴿قُلُوبُكُما﴾ its fāʿil, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, and the clause «صغت» gives the reason, with no grammatical position; and the meaning of «صغت» is «مالت» (inclined). ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿إِنْ تَظاهَرا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «إن تتوبا», and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being «يجد ناصرا» (he will find a helper); ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb. ﴿فَإِنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of reason; ﴿إن اللَّهِ﴾ «إنّ» and its noun «[Translator's note: the Name of Majesty is printed with a kasra in the source; in the verse it is «اللَّهَ», the accusative noun of «إنّ».]»; ﴿هُوَ﴾ a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿مَوْلاهُ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ», and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَجِبْرِيلُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿وَصالِحُ﴾ conjoined to «جبريل»; ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿وَالْمَلائِكَةُ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿بَعْدَ ذلِكَ﴾ an adverb of time annexed to the demonstrative; ﴿ظَهِيرٌ﴾ the khabar for what has preceded.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿عَسى﴾ a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb, one of the verbs of hope; ﴿رَبُّهُ﴾ its noun; ﴿إِنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ﴾ «إن» is conditional and makes the verb jussive, and a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted; ﴿أَنْ يُبْدِلَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by «أن», the hāʾ being the first object, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and what follows it is the khabar (predicate) of «عسى»; ﴿أَزْواجاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿خَيْراً﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «أزواجا»; ﴿مِنْكُنَّ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خيرا»; ﴿مُسْلِماتٍ، مُؤْمِناتٍ، قانِتاتٍ، تائِباتٍ، عابِداتٍ، سائِحاتٍ، ثَيِّباتٍ﴾ multiple naʿts of «أزواجا»; ﴿وَأَبْكاراً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ﴾ its i'rab has been given before; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the vocative clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿قُوا﴾ an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil; ﴿أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَأَهْلِيكُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «أنفسكم»; ﴿ناراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «نارا»; ﴿وَالْحِجارَةُ﴾ conjoined to «الناس»; ﴿عَلَيْها﴾ a fronted khabar; ﴿مَلائِكَةٌ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is a second naʿt of «نارا»; ﴿غِلاظٌ شِدادٌ﴾ two naʿts of «ملائكة»; ﴿لا﴾ negating; ﴿يَعْصُونَ اللَّهَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil and the Name of Majesty its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿ما﴾ a badal (substitute) for the Name of Majesty, and the clause is a third naʿt; ﴿أَمَرَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَيَفْعَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿يُؤْمَرُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is the ṣila of «ما».

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ﴾ its i'rab has been given before; ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين»; ﴿لا تَعْتَذِرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive «لا», the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is the object of an omitted saying (maqūl qawl maḥdhūf). ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining [«ما»] and the restrained [«إنّ»] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); ﴿تُجْزَوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿ما﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ «كان» and its noun, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «كنتم».

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: its i'rab has been given before; ﴿تُوبُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿تَوْبَةً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿نَصُوحاً﴾ a naʿt (adjective); ﴿عَسى﴾ a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb; ﴿رَبُّكُمْ﴾ the noun of «عسى»; ﴿أَنْ يُكَفِّرَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by «أن», and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of an accusative as the khabar (predicate) of «عسى»; ﴿عَنْكُمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿سَيِّئاتِكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its first object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir), and the clause is conjoined to «يكفر»; ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb; ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil, and the clause is a naʿt of «جنات»; ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿لا﴾ negating; ﴿يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «النبي»; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مَعَهُ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿نُورُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَسْعى﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ an adverb of place annexed to «أيديهم»; ﴿وَبِأَيْمانِهِمْ﴾ both are conjoined to the adverb; ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl; ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf); ﴿أَتْمِمْ﴾ a verb of supplication whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿لَنا﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿نُورَنا﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the two clauses are the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿وَاغْفِرْ لَنا﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾ «إنّ» and its noun; ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ both are attached to «قدير»; ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿قَدِيرٌ﴾ the khabar of «إنّ», and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya).

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ﴾ its i'rab has been given before. ﴿جاهِدِ الْكُفَّارَ﴾ an imperative verb, «الكفار» being its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَالْمُنافِقِينَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الكفار»; ﴿وَاغْلُظْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَمَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is circumstantial (a ḥāl); ﴿وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿امْرَأَتَ نُوحٍ﴾ a badal (substitute), annexed to «نوح»; ﴿وَامْرَأَتَ لُوطٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿كانَتا﴾ «كان» and its noun; ﴿تَحْتَ﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of «كان»; ﴿عَبْدَيْنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿مِنْ﴾ ﴿عِبادِنا﴾ both are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «عبدين»; ﴿صالِحَيْنِ﴾ a naʿt of «عبدين», and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَخانَتاهُما﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَلَمْ يُغْنِيا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the alif being its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿عَنْهُما﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ ḥāl; ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَقِيلَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿ادْخُلَا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿النَّارَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿الدَّاخِلِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا امْرَأَتَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾: the i'rab of its like has been given before. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿قالَتْ رَبِّ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, which has been dropped; ﴿ابْنِ﴾ a verb of supplication, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, the fāʿil being latent, and the two clauses are the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause «قالت» is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿لِي﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ابن»; ﴿عِنْدَكَ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿بَيْتاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فِي الْجَنَّةِ﴾ both are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective); ﴿وَنَجِّنِي﴾ a verb of supplication and its mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being latent; ﴿مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَعَمَلِهِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; ﴿وَنَجِّنِي مِنَ الْقَوْمِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ a naʿt of «القوم».

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَمَرْيَمَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «امرأة فرعون»; ﴿ابْنَتَ عِمْرانَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «مريم», annexed to «عمران»; ﴿الَّتِي﴾ also a naʿt of «مريم»; ﴿أَحْصَنَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿فَرْجَها﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فَنَفَخْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فِيهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿مِنْ رُوحِنا﴾ both are attached to the verb as well. ﴿وَصَدَّقَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿بِكَلِماتِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿رَبِّها﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿وَكُتُبِهِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَكانَتْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent; ﴿مِنَ الْقانِتِينَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of «كانت», and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

farraa:1-2.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَآ أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكَ﴾.
It came down concerning Māriya the Copt. The Prophet ﷺ used to assign a day to each of his wives. When it was ʿĀʾisha's day, Ḥafṣa bint ʿUmar visited her, so her [Ḥafṣa's] house was empty, and the Prophet ﷺ sent for Māriya the Copt, and she was with the Prophet ﷺ in Ḥafṣa's dwelling. Ḥafṣa came to her dwelling and found the curtain let down. The Prophet ﷺ came out and said: Will you keep this secret for me? She said: Yes. He said: Then she is forbidden to me — meaning Māriya — and I tell you that your father and Abū Bakr will rule after me. Ḥafṣa told ʿĀʾisha the news, and revelation came down to the Prophet ﷺ about it. He called Ḥafṣa and said: What made you do what you did? She said to him: And who told you that I said that to ʿĀʾisha? He said: "The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me". Then he divorced Ḥafṣa with one divorce and kept away from his wives for twenty-nine days. And there came down to him: ﴿لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَآ أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكَ﴾, regarding intimacy with Māriya. Then He said: ﴿قَدْ فَرَضَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ تَحِلَّةَ أَيْمَانِكُمْ﴾, meaning: the expiation of your oaths. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ freed a slave and returned to Māriya.
[Al-Farrāʾ] said: Ḥibbān told me this interpretation from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās. Then He said: "عرف بعضه" — He is saying: he made Ḥafṣa aware of part of what was said and left part. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read "عَرَف", light.
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl al-Marwazī told me, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī: "عَرَف", light.
Al-Farrāʾ told us: and a shaykh of Banū Asad — meaning al-Kisāʾī — told me, from Nuʿaym, from Abū ʿAmr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: when a man recited to him "عَرَّف بعضه" with doubling, he would pelt him with pebbles. It is as if those who say عَرَف, light, mean: he was angered by it and requited it, as you say to a man who wrongs you: By Allah, I will surely "know" that against you (i.e. repay you for it). And by my life, he did requite Ḥafṣa by divorcing her; and this is a good interpretation. [And it is reported of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī that he read عَرَف light, like Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.]

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلاً لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾.
This is a parable by which ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa are meant; He struck the parable for them both, saying: The faith of their husbands did not benefit the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot, and their hypocrisy did not harm their husbands; likewise the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ would not benefit you two if you did not believe, and your sins would not harm him. Then He said: ﴿وضَرَبَ اللهُ مَثَلاً لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا امْرَأَتَ فِرْعَوْن﴾, so He commanded them both to be like Āsiya and like Mary daughter of ʿImrān, who guarded her chastity (farj). Al-farj here is the neck-opening of her shift; it is mentioned that Jibrīl ﷺ blew into the opening of her garment. Every opening in a shift, whether a tear or otherwise, can be called farj. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَالَهَا مِنْ فُرُوجٍ﴾, meaning the sky has no cracks or rifts.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿إِن تَتُوبَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾.
He means ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa. That is because ʿĀʾisha said: O Messenger of Allah, as for the day of the others, you complete it, but on my day you do what you did? So there came down: "If you two repent to Allah" from your collaborating against the Prophet ﷺ ﴿فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا﴾: they have deviated and inclined. ﴿وَإِن تَظَاهَرَا عَلَيْهِ﴾: [if] you collaborate against him. ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it light, and the people of the Hijaz read it: "تظَّاهرا" with doubling. ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ مَوْلاَهُ﴾: his protector against you both, ﴿وَجِبْرِيلُ وَصَالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: such as Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, in whom there is no hypocrisy. Then He said: ﴿وَالْمَلاَئِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ﴾: after those, He means helpers, and He did not say ظهراء. If someone said that ظهير belongs to Jibrīl, the righteous believers and the angels [together], it would be correct; but it is good to make ظهير belong to the angels specifically, because of His saying (والملائكة) — after the help of these — [are] ظهير.
As for His saying: ﴿وَصَالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, it is singular in the sense of a plural, as you say: لا يأتينى إلا سائس الحرب (none shall come to me except the manager of war): whoever is capable of managing war has been told to come, whether one or more. Similar to it: ﴿وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُمَا﴾: this is general [201/b], not one or two. Likewise His saying: ﴿والَّلذانِ يأْتِيَانِهَا مِنكُمْ فَآذُوهما﴾, and likewise: ﴿إنّ الإِنْسَانَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ﴾ and ﴿إِنَّ الإِنْسَانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً﴾ — in much of the Qur'an the singular conveys the meaning of the plural.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read: "أنْ يُبْدلَهُ", light, and the people of the Hijaz read: "أن يبَدِّله" [with doubling]; and both are correct: أبدلت and بدّلت.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿سَائِحَاتٍ﴾.
They are women who fast. He said: We think that the one who fasts is called سائح (wanderer) only because the wanderer has no provisions with him and eats only where he finds [food], so it is as if it were taken from that. And Allah knows best.
The Arabs say of a horse when it stands without fodder: صائم (fasting). That is because it has two meals, a meal in the morning and a meal in the evening, so it is likened to the predawn meal of a human being and his breaking of the fast.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿قُوۤاْ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ﴾.
Teach your families that by which they ward off sins; teach them that.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿تَوْبَةً نَّصُوحاً﴾.
The people of Medina and al-Aʿmash read it with fatḥa on the nūn, and it is reported of ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan [that they read] "نُصُوحاً" with ḍamma on the nūn. It is as if those who say "نُصوحاً" intend the maṣdar (verbal noun), like قُعودا, while those who say "نَصوحا" make it a description of the repentance. Its meaning is: when he repents of that sin, he resolves in himself never to return to it.
His saying: ﴿يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا﴾.
Not everyone who enters Paradise says this; only the lowest of them in rank says it. That is because the foremost, as has been mentioned, pass over the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ) like lightning, some like the wind, some like a swift horse, and some crawling and creeping. It is these who say: ﴿رَبَّنَا أتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا﴾ so that we may be saved.
If a reader read "ويدخلْكم" in the jussive, it would be a valid way, because the answer [is] to عسى: the فاء is implied in [the answer to] عسى, and "entering" is intended as conjoined to the place of the فاء. But no one read it so. Similar to it: ﴿فَأَصَّدَقَ وأكُنْ مِنَ الصَّالِحِين﴾.
Similar is the poet's saying:
فأبلونى بليتكُم لعلى * أصالحكم، واستدرجْ نَويَّا
(So grant me your favour, perhaps I may make peace with you, and draw my distant company [back] step by step.)
He put it in the jussive because he intended joining it back to لعلّى.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Taḥrīm (The Prohibition)
Medinan
﷽
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ ما أحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ تَبْتَغِي مَرْضاتَ أزْواجِكَ واللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ means: Allah has forgiven you that prohibition. It has come in the exegesis that the Prophet ﷺ drank honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, and ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa agreed to say to him: "We smell on you the odour of maghāfīr." ”اَلْمَغافِيرُ“ is a gum with an altered smell; and it is said in the exegesis that it is a herb. When he came to each of them, she said to him: "I smell on you the odour of maghāfīr." So the Prophet ﷺ forbade himself the drinking of honey; and it is said that he swore to that. And it has come in the exegesis — and this is the more widely held — that the Prophet ﷺ «was alone, on a day belonging to ʿĀʾisha, with his slave-girl, the mother of Ibrāhīm, who was called "Māriya the Copt." Ḥafṣa came upon that, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "Do not inform ʿĀʾisha of that." She said to him: "I will not." And he forbade Māriya to himself — and it is said that he also swore along with that. Then Ḥafṣa informed ʿĀʾisha of the news and asked her to keep it secret; and Allah acquainted His Prophet with that, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَإذْ أسَرَّ النَّبِيُّ إلى بَعْضِ أزْواجِهِ حَدِيثًا﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3]», meaning Ḥafṣa. The position of ”إذْ“ is accusative, as though He said: "And remember when the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives," meaning Ḥafṣa. ﴿فَلَمّا نَبَّأتْ بِهِ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3] means: when she told ʿĀʾisha of it.

﴿وَأظْهَرَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ وأعْرَضَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3] — it was also read ”عَرَفَ بَعْضَهُ“, with the rāʾ undoubled. And Allah made known that the prohibition, according to this exegesis, does not make (the thing) forbidden, and He said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ ما أحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ تَبْتَغِي مَرْضاتَ أزْواجِكَ﴾. So Allah did not grant His Prophet the right to forbid anything except what Allah has forbidden; and according to both of these exegeses no one may forbid what Allah has made lawful. Then Allah said: ﴿قَدْ فَرَضَ اللَّهُ لَكم تَحِلَّةَ أيْمانِكُمْ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 2], meaning the expiation, because it has been transmitted that he swore along with that prohibition; and some said the expiation is the expiation for the prohibition (itself). As for ﴿عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3], its interpretation is that he made Ḥafṣa aware of part of it. ﴿وَأعْرَضَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3]: it has come in the exegesis that when he forbade Māriya (to himself), he told Ḥafṣa that after him Abū Bakr and ʿUmar would rule; so he made her aware of part of the news she had divulged and turned away from part. For the Prophet ﷺ had made known everything he had confided [Translator's note: so printed (عَرَّفَ); the argument seems to require "knew" (عَرَفَ)], and turning away can only be from what is known. The interpretation of this in the language is good and clear: the meaning of ﴿عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3] is "he requited (her) for it," as you say to someone you are threatening: "I know what you did, I am aware of what you have done," its meaning being "so I will requite you for it," not that you intend merely that you know. Like it is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَما تَفْعَلُوا مِن خَيْرٍ يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Baqara: 197], whose interpretation is: Allah knows it and requites it — for Allah knows everything that is done. Like it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ ما في قُلُوبِهِمْ فَأعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 63], while Allah knows what is in the hearts of all creatures. And like it is His saying: ﴿فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ﴾ [al-Zalzala: 7]: the point is not that he sees what he did; he only sees the recompense of what he did. It is said that the Prophet ﷺ divorced Ḥafṣa with a single pronouncement, and that was her recompense in his view; that is the interpretation of ﴿عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ وأعْرَضَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3], i.e. he requited (her) for part of the matter. Ḥafṣa was much given to fasting and to standing in prayer at night, so Allah the Exalted commanded him to take her back, and he took her back.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿إنْ تَتُوبا إلى اللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُما﴾ — He means by it ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa. The meaning of ﴿صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُما﴾ is: your hearts have swerved and deviated from truthfulness.

His saying: ﴿وَإنْ تَظاهَرا عَلَيْهِ فَإنَّ اللَّهَ هو مَوْلاهُ﴾ means: (if) you two support one another against him, then Allah is his protector (mawlā), i.e. He undertakes his support. ﴿وَجِبْرِيلُ وصالِحُ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that "the righteous of the believers" are Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; it has also come in the exegesis that the righteous of the believers is ʿUmar; and it is said that the righteous of the believers are the best of the Muslims. ”صالِحُ“ here stands for the plural, as you say: "The good one among people does this," meaning every good person. ﴿والمَلائِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ﴾ — in the sense of ”ظُهَراءُ“ (supporters), i.e. the angels too are helpers of the Prophet ﷺ.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿عَسى رَبُّهُ إنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ أنْ يُبْدِلَهُ أزْواجًا خَيْرًا مِنكُنَّ مُسْلِماتٍ﴾ — it was also read ”يُبَدِّلَهُ“, with a doubled dāl and a fatḥa on the bāʾ; ”يُبَدِّلَهُ“ is for intensiveness. Both are good, and it has been read so.

His saying: ﴿قانِتاتٍ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis: obedient. ”اَلْقُنُوتُ“ is performing what brings one near to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿سائِحاتٍ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis from the Prophet ﷺ «that the sāʾiḥūn are those who fast», and this is among what is in the earlier scriptures. The lexicographers said: the one fasting was only called ”سائِحٌ“ (a wanderer) because the one who wanders is devoted to worship and has no provisions with him, so when he finds provisions he eats; and the one fasting likewise spends the day without eating anything. Because of his resemblance to him he was called ”سائِحًا“.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قُوا أنْفُسَكم وأهْلِيكم نارًا﴾ means: hold yourselves and your families to what brings one near to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and keep yourselves and your families away from acts of disobedience. The meaning of ﴿قُوا أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ is: guard (waqqū) yourselves. It has come in the exegesis: "May Allah have mercy on a man who says: 'O my family, your prayer, your fasting, your poor, your orphan, your neighbours!'" — meaning: keep to and preserve your prayer and these things mentioned; fulfil Allah's obligation in them. And in the hadith: «"Perhaps Allah will gather them with him in Paradise."»

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَقُودُها النّاسُ والحِجارَةُ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that they are stones of sulphur. ”اَلْوَقُودُ“, with a fatḥa on the wāw, is that with which fire is kindled, firewood and the like; one says ”وَقَدْتُ النّارَ، وُقُودًا“ (I kindled the fire), with a ḍamma on the wāw.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا تُوبُوا إلى اللَّهِ تَوْبَةً نَصُوحًا﴾ — with a fatḥa on the nūn; it is also read ”نُصُوحًا“ with a ḍamma on the nūn. Whoever gives the fatḥa takes it as a naʿt (adjective) of the repentance, meaning "a repentance consummate in sincerity"; ”فَعُولٌ“ is one of the agent forms used for intensiveness in description: you say "a man patient (ṣabūr) and grateful (shakūr)" and "a sincere repentance (tawba naṣūḥ)." Whoever read ”نُصُوحًا“ with a ḍamma on the nūn, its meaning is "they are sincere in this with sincerity (nuṣūḥ)"; one says ”نَصَحْتُ لَهُ نُصْحًا، ونِصاحَةً، ونُصُوحًا“ (I was sincere to him).

It has come in the exegesis that the sincere repentance is that after which the penitent does not return to the sin; and some of them said: that with which he does not intend to return to the sin.

His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ لا يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ﴾ — ”يَوْمَ“ is accusative through His saying: ﴿عَسى رَبُّكم أنْ يُكَفِّرَ عَنْكم سَيِّئاتِكم ويُدْخِلَكم جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ يَوْمَ لا يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ﴾, i.e. on that day. The reading is the accusative in His saying ﴿وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ﴾, conjoined to ﴿أنْ يُكَفِّرَ﴾; had it been read with the jussive, that would be a valid way, construed on the position of ﴿عَسى رَبُّكم أنْ يُكَفِّرَ عَنْكم سَيِّئاتِكُمْ﴾, because ”عَسى“ from Allah is binding. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَإنِّي لَغَفّارٌ لِمَن تابَ وآمَنَ وعَمِلَ صالِحًا ثُمَّ اهْتَدى﴾ [Ṭāhā: 82]. And His saying: ﴿نُورُهم يَسْعى بَيْنَ أيْدِيهِمْ وبِأيْمانِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا أتْمِمْ لَنا نُورَنا﴾ means: when the believers see the light of the hypocrites being extinguished, they ask Allah to perfect their light for them.

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلا لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا امْرَأتَ نُوحٍ وامْرَأتَ لُوطٍ كانَتا تَحْتَ عَبْدَيْنِ مِن عِبادِنا صالِحَيْنِ فَخانَتاهُما فَلَمْ يُغْنِيا عَنْهُما مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا﴾ — Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the prophets avail nothing for one who commits acts of disobedience. It has come in the exegesis that their betrayal was not in harlotry, because Allah does not afflict the prophets with corruption in their wives. It is said that the betrayal of Lūṭ's wife was that she used to point out the guests, and the betrayal of Nūḥ's wife was that she used to say he was mad — Allah bless him and all His prophets. Whoever claims otherwise is mistaken; for some of those who interpreted His saying ﴿يا نُوحُ إنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِن أهْلِكَ إنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صالِحٍ﴾ [Hūd: 46] inclined to a kind of corruption. The reading here is ”عَمِلَ غَيْرَ صالِحٍ“ and ﴿عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صالِحٍ﴾ [Hūd: 46], and both come back to one meaning: the interpretation of ﴿إنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صالِحٍ﴾ [Hūd: 46] is "he is one of unrighteous deeds." Whoever disbelieves, his kinship with his believing family is cut off: he does not inherit from them, nor do they inherit from him.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا امْرَأتَ فِرْعَوْنَ إذْ قالَتْ رَبِّ ابْنِ لِي عِنْدَكَ بَيْتًا في الجَنَّةِ ونَجِّنِي مِن فِرْعَوْنَ وعَمَلِهِ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that Pharaoh drove four stakes for her, bound her body and her legs, placed a millstone on her chest and put her in the sun; and that Allah gave her relief, and she saw her house in Paradise. It has also come in the exegesis that the angels used to shade her from the sun with their wings.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَرْيَمَ ابْنَتَ عِمْرانَ الَّتِي أحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَها فَنَفَخْنا فِيهِ مِن رُوحِنا وصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِماتِ رَبِّها وكُتُبِهِ﴾ — it was also read ”وَكِتابِهِ“. ﴿أحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَها﴾: it has come in the exegesis that what is meant by it is the opening of her garment. The Arabs say of a chaste man: "He is clean of garment" and "He is good of waistband (ḥujza)," meaning that he is chaste. They recited the verse of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
؎رِقاقُ النِّعالِ طَيِّبٌ حُجُزاتُهم ∗∗∗ يُحَيُّونَ بِالرَّيْحانِ يَوْمَ السَّباسِبِ
(Fine of sandals, good of waistbands, they are greeted with sweet basil on the day of al-Sabāsib.)
They explained ”طَيِّبٌ حُجُزاتُهُمْ“ as meaning that they are chaste. Likewise ﴿فَنَفَخْنا فِيهِ مِن رُوحِنا﴾ means: into the opening of her garment.
